pr_body:
When the SAS token is prefixed with ? the SDK parses incorrectly
all the query params and removes the first query param, this
produces an invalid signature preventing the repository to
authenticate against the storage service. This commit reverts
to the previous behaviour where the SAS token was appended to
the URL as it is provided by the user.

Closes #88140
pr_title: Use the provided SAS token without SDK sanitation that can produce invalid signatures
pr_comment: Hi @fcofdez, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
The CI failures seems to be infrastructure related, this is ready for review.

review_comment: I believe `exchange` needs to be closed after we finished writing the response.
I believe there an issue with that because the SDK doesn't export these classes in `module-info`, but I'm not sure whether we enforce it.
We were using the `StorageConnectionString` class already. I agree that we should move to our own connection string parsing, but we can defer that.

FYI.
The fix for your problem will go out with next storage release.
See https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-java/issues/29998
https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-java/pull/30003

When the fix is out I suggest to not use types from `*.implementation.*` - we don't export them in our modules - which might be a problem on latest java runtime versions.

If there's anything else we can do to help here, please let us know.
Thanks for the heads up @kasobol-msft. I noticed that we're using a few implementation details, I'll tackle that once we upgrade to the new version.
